title: Exploiting the Lithosphere: Mining
seo_title: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Exploiting the Lithosphere: Mining Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 11 Physical Sciences: Exploiting the lithosphere
standard_text: The lithosphere as a source of minerals; mining and mineral processing: the history and processes of gold mining in South Africa (Witwatersrand), extraction of gold with cyanide; extraction of iron and phosphates; the environmental impact of mining, including acid mine drainage. (summary of CAPS Physical Sciences, Grade 11, Chemistry: Exploiting the lithosphere)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Physical Sciences worksheets (CAPS): minerals and ores, gold mining on the Witwatersrand, extracting gold and iron, and the environmental impact of mining. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: An ore is a rock from which a metal can be extracted at a profit.
key_sub: Gold is dissolved out of crushed ore with cyanide.
body_html:
How to think about it

The lithosphere contains the minerals that South Africa's economy depends on: gold, platinum, coal, iron ore and phosphates. Gold was discovered on the Witwatersrand in 1886; it is found in conglomerate reefs that run several kilometres underground.

Gold ore is crushed and milled, leached with cyanide solution, and the gold is recovered with zinc or activated carbon. Iron is extracted from haematite by reduction in a blast furnace. Mining creates jobs and export income but also causes mine dumps, dust, loss of habitat and acid mine drainage.

Example

An ore has 5 g of gold per tonne. Gold in 1 000 t?

5 g/t × 1 000 t

Answer: 5 kg

Example

What causes acid mine drainage?

Pyrite + air + water

Answer: sulfuric acid formed from pyrite

Common mistakes

  • Thinking gold is mined as nuggets.
  • Thinking mining has only positive effects.
  • Thinking all rocks with metal are ores.

faq.a: It is very poisonous, so cyanide waste must be treated before it reaches rivers.

faq.q: What is done to old mine dumps?
faq.a: They are re-mined for leftover gold, or covered with soil and plants to stop dust and erosion.

items.q: Which method is used to explore for ore bodies by measuring small differences in gravity or magnetism?
items.e: Drilling then confirms the ore.

items.q: How did black coal in the Bowen and Cape Town Basins form?
c: plant material from ancient swamps was buried and changed by heat and pressure over millions of years
items.e: Most is Permian, about 250–300 million years old.

items.q: Elna reads about a resource that formed from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers). Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how groundwater formed.

items.q: When is open-cut mining used rather than underground mining?
c: when the ore is very deep and narrow
when the ore is large and close to the surface
items.e: The Super Pit at Kalgoorlie is open-cut.

items.q: How did the rock of the Organ Pipes in Victoria form?
c: from lava that cooled slowly and cracked into columns
from magma that cooled slowly deep underground
from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together
from sand and gravel eroded from ancient mountains, then pressed and cemented
items.e: The Organ Pipes in Victoria is basalt (igneous).

items.q: Liam asks how coal formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
items.e: Coal formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years.

items.q: Why can a deposit that was not ore become ore?
c: a rise in metal price or a cheaper mining method makes it profitable
the metal grows in the rock
the deposit moves closer to the surface
items.e: Economics defines ore.

items.q: Priya reads about a resource that formed from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how coal formed.

items.q: Amahle asks how rock salt formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
items.e: Rock salt formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago.

items.q: Why are fossil fuels called non-renewable?
c: they form over millions of years, far slower than we use them
they are found only in deserts
items.e: Coal, oil and gas are non-renewable.

items.q: How did the rock of Kata Tjuta form?
c: from lava that cooled slowly and cracked into columns
from magma that cooled slowly deep underground
from rounded pebbles and boulders cemented together
from mudstone changed by heat and pressure
items.e: Kata Tjuta is conglomerate (sedimentary).

items.q: Jabu reads about a resource that formed from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how rock salt formed.

items.q: Bongani reads about a resource that formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how oil and natural gas formed.

items.q: Why is a cap rock needed for an oil or gas reservoir?
c: it is impermeable, so it stops the oil and gas escaping upwards
items.e: Shale and salt are common cap rocks.

items.q: Kgomotso reads about a resource that formed from iron that settled out of ancient oceans in layers. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how iron ore formed.

items.q: What is mineral processing (beneficiation)?
c: crushing ore and separating the valuable mineral from the waste rock
items.e: Flotation separates many sulfide minerals.

items.q: Lindiwe asks how oil and natural gas formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
items.e: Oil and natural gas formed from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years.

items.q: How do oil and natural gas form?
c: remains of marine plankton are buried, heated and changed into hydrocarbons, which collect in traps
items.e: They need a source rock, reservoir rock and cap rock.

items.q: What kind of rock is the Organ Pipes in Victoria made of?
items.e: It formed from lava that cooled slowly and cracked into columns.

items.q: Chloe asks how groundwater formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers)
from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
items.e: Groundwater formed from rain and snowmelt soaking into porous rock and sediment (aquifers).

items.q: Where is most of South Africa's gold found?
items.e: Gold was discovered on the Witwatersrand in 1 886.

items.q: How is gold recovered from the cyanide solution?
c: by adding zinc (or using activated carbon), which displaces the gold
items.e: Zinc is more reactive and displaces gold from solution.

items.q: An ore contains 4 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 1 000 tonnes of ore?
An ore contains 4 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 2 500 tonnes of ore?
What are mine dumps?
c: large heaps of waste rock and tailings left after extraction
items.e: The dumps around Johannesburg are mine waste.

items.q: In the reaction 2[Au(CN)₂]⁻ + Zn → 2Au + [Zn(CN)₄]²⁻, what is oxidised?
items.e: Zinc loses electrons to become Zn²⁺.

items.q: South Africa has the world's largest reserves of which metals?
items.e: They are found in the Bushveld Complex.

items.q: A mine extracts 40 kg of gold from 5 000 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 40 000 g ÷ 5 000 t = 8 g per tonne.

items.q: In which kind of mining is ore removed from a large pit at the surface?
items.e: Open-cast mining is used when the ore is near the surface.

items.q: Why must South African gold mines be very deep?
c: gold is only found in the mantle
the gold-bearing reefs slope down to depths of several kilometres
items.e: Some mines are more than 3 km deep.

items.q: Why is iron extracted in a blast furnace with carbon (coke)?
c: carbon is less reactive than iron
carbon is more reactive than iron and removes oxygen from the iron oxide
items.e: Fe₂O₃ is reduced to Fe by carbon monoxide.

items.q: A mine extracts 3 kg of gold from 500 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 3 000 g ÷ 500 t = 6 g per tonne.

items.q: Which metal is extracted from haematite?
items.e: Haematite is iron(III) oxide, Fe₂O₃.

items.q: A mine extracts 6 kg of gold from 1 000 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 6 000 g ÷ 1 000 t = 6 g per tonne.

items.q: An ore contains 3 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 800 tonnes of ore?
An ore contains 8 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 1500 tonnes of ore?
In which kind of mining are shafts and tunnels dug to reach the ore?
items.e: Gold on the Witwatersrand is mined underground.

items.q: An ore contains 8 g of gold per tonne. How much gold can be extracted from 1 000 tonnes of ore?
A mine extracts 10 kg of gold from 2000 tonnes of ore. What is the grade of the ore?
items.e: Grade = 10 000 g ÷ 2 000 t = 5 g per tonne.

items.q: In which kind of rock is Witwatersrand gold found?
items.e: The gold-bearing conglomerate layers are called reefs.

items.q: Chloe learns that an aquifer holds 800 billion litres. People pump out 25 billion litres a year, and rain refills only a small amount. About how many years until it runs low (ignoring refill)?
items.e: 800 ÷ 25 = 32 years. Pumping faster than refilling depletes groundwater.

items.q: Dumisani's town has 2 000 people who each use 4 kg of rubbish per person each day. If everyone cuts use in half, what is the new total?
items.e: Halving use per person halves the total, even with the same population.

items.q: Musa's town has 10 000 people who each use 4 kg of rubbish per person each day. If the population doubles and each person uses the same amount, what is the new total?
items.e: Twice the people × the same use = twice the total.

items.q: Nadia's town has 1 000 people who each use 4 kg of rubbish per person each day. If the population doubles and each person uses the same amount, what is the new total?
items.e: Twice the people × the same use = twice the total.

What is an environmental impact assessment (EIA)?
c: a test of the soil after a mine closes
a study of the likely effects of a project on the environment before it is approved
items.e: It considers alternatives and ways to reduce harm.

items.q: Why is dust from mine dumps a health problem?
c: the dust makes rain more acidic only
fine dust can damage lungs and may contain toxic or radioactive metals
the dust has too much oxygen
items.e: Some dumps contain uranium and heavy metals.

items.q: What is rehabilitation of a mine site?
c: restoring the land after mining, for example by covering dumps with soil and plants
items.e: Plants stop dust and erosion.

items.q: Which is a negative effect of mining on the environment?
c: loss of habitat and pollution of water and air
items.e: Mining disturbs land and can pollute water.

items.q: Why does Traditional Owners' knowledge matter in managing land?
c: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples have tens of thousands of years of knowledge of country, such as cultural burning
items.e: Indigenous rangers manage large areas.

items.q: Which mineral reacts with air and water to cause acid mine drainage?
items.e: Oxidised pyrite forms sulfuric acid.

items.q: Which is a positive effect of mining on South Africa's economy?
c: it provides jobs and export income
it removes the need for roads
items.e: Mining is a major employer and earns foreign exchange.

items.q: Name one effect of acid mine drainage.
c: it pollutes rivers and kills fish and plants
it raises the price of gold
items.e: The acid and dissolved metals harm living things.

items.q: How can acid mine drainage be treated?
c: by pumping it into dams without treatment
by neutralising it with lime (calcium hydroxide)
items.e: Lime raises the pH and makes metals settle out.

items.q: What type of rock is schist?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: What type of rock is granite?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: Mudstone or shale is heated and squeezed deep underground without melting. Which rock forms?
items.e: Metamorphism.

items.q: How does sediment become sedimentary rock?
c: It is heated until it glows.
Layers are squashed (compaction) and stuck together (cementation).
items.e: Over millions of years.

items.q: How does bauxite form?
c: intense weathering in a hot, wet climate leaches other minerals and leaves aluminium oxides
items.e: It is a residual deposit.

items.q: An ore body contains 10 000 tonnes of ore with a grade of 62% iron. How many tonnes of iron does it contain?
Processing 200 t of ore produces 8 t of copper. What is the ore grade, as a percentage?
A deposit holds 2000 million tonnes. Production is 40 million tonnes a year, but a new mine will raise it by 2%. Using the higher rate, about how long will the deposit last?
items.e: New rate = 40 × 1,02 = 40,8 Mt per year; 2000 ÷ 40,8 = 49 years.

items.q: A deposit holds 4 000 million tonnes. Production is 40 million tonnes a year, but a new mine will raise it by 2%. Using the higher rate, about how long will the deposit last?
items.e: New rate = 40 × 1,02 = 40,8 Mt per year; 4 000 ÷ 40,8 = 98 years.

items.q: A gold ore has a grade of 4 g per tonne. How many tonnes of ore must be processed to obtain 62,2 g of gold?
items.e: Ore = gold ÷ grade = 62,2 ÷ 4 = 15,6 t.

items.q: Limestone is heated and squeezed deep underground without melting. Which rock forms?
items.e: Metamorphism.

items.q: What type of rock is chalk?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: What type of rock is basalt?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: Which rock is slate made from when it is changed by heat and pressure?
items.e: Metamorphic rocks form from other rocks.

items.q: Processing 200 t of ore produces 2 t of copper. What is the ore grade, as a percentage?
A gold ore has a grade of 3 g per tonne. How many tonnes of ore must be processed to obtain 311 g of gold?
items.e: Ore = gold ÷ grade = 311 ÷ 3 = 104 t.

items.q: What type of rock is pumice?
items.e: Igneous: cooled magma or lava. Sedimentary: layers of sediment. Metamorphic: changed by heat and pressure.

items.q: How do metamorphic rocks form?
c: Existing rock is changed by heat and pressure without melting.
items.e: Marble, slate.

items.q: An ore body contains 5 000 tonnes of ore with a grade of 0,8% copper. How many tonnes of copper does it contain?
A gold ore has a grade of 3 g per tonne. How many tonnes of ore must be processed to obtain 31,1 g of gold?
items.e: Ore = gold ÷ grade = 31,1 ÷ 3 = 10,4 t.
